items.text: Team state has shifted since round 1: all 6 existing teams are now enabled: false (round 1 showed director-swarm and scenario-qa as enabled). The conclusion's Finding 5 now flags that draft objectives/KPIs need a verification pass during execution since they were written assuming active teams.

The Team struct has evolved since the original spec was written. The flat SpawnMode field is gone — the Team now holds Runtime (from teamconfig), Coordination, and Execution sub-structs. See api/store/models.go:86-100 and api/teamconfig/config.go. V2 fields coexist with this structure cleanly (all additive).

HEARTBEAT.md and RESPONSIBILITIES.md live at teams/<team>/members/<agent>/ — per-agent, not per-team. Dependency computation that scans these files must aggregate references across all members of a team.

A graph infrastructure already exists at scenarios/prompt-manager/api/graph/ with node types (team, agent, skill, cli) and edge types (membership, cli-read, bold-listed, default-scope, path-ref, code-usage). The team-dependencies command can be implemented as a projection over this graph — no new stored edge kind needed, no new scanner logic.

The prompt builder already has a precedent for rendering team JSON fields as natural-language markdown: buildCoordinationSkillSection (prompt_builder.go:298) reads Runtime.Mode, Coordination.Pattern, Execution.QueuePolicy, DecisionMode and emits a '# Team Coordination' markdown section. The new v2 fields should follow this exact pattern.

team_store.go:77 writes the global CurrentSchemaVersion constant into each team.json on Create. Per the round 1 d2 decision (per-file versioning), the implementation must switch to writing a Team-specific constant (TeamSchemaVersion = 2) while leaving the global constant at 1 for other entities.

items.topic: Placement of the v2 team-profile section in heartbeat prompts
items.context: The v2 fields (Mission, Objectives, KPIs, Consumers, Contributions) will render as a markdown section in the heartbeat prompt. The current section order (prompt_builder.go:140-200) is: Team Charter (TEAM.md) → Responsibilities (per-member) → Team Org Context → Team Coordination → ... → HEARTBEAT.md. The new team-profile section needs a home in this sequence.

options.label: Place '# Team Profile' immediately AFTER '# Team Charter (shared/TEAM.md)' and BEFORE '# Team Responsibilities'
options.rationale: Profile (structured mission/objectives/KPIs/consumers/contributions) is the natural complement to the Charter (freeform narrative). Keeping them adjacent gives the agent the full team briefing at the top of the prompt before drilling into individual-agent responsibilities.

options.label: Place '# Team Profile' after '# Team Coordination' (near end, alongside execution policies)
options.rationale: Groups all structured team.json-derived content together. But separates profile from charter, which makes the reading order less intuitive.

options.label: Merge v2 fields into the existing Team Charter section (render before the TEAM.md content)
options.rationale: One section for all team-level context. Downside: conflates structured data with freeform, and modifies an existing section instead of adding a clean new one.

items.topic: Draft value handling in the execution item
items.context: Round 1 produced draft objectives/KPIs/consumers/contributions for all 6 teams. Team state has shifted (all disabled now) and the draft values reflect the earlier state. The execution action needs clear direction on how much rework to do.

options.label: Execution agent re-audits each TEAM.md and updates drafts as needed before committing v2 values
options.rationale: Ensures v2 values reflect current team charters, not a stale snapshot. Small extra effort; high correctness. The research conclusion already instructs this in Finding 5 and Action 1.

options.label: Commit round 1 drafts verbatim; refinement happens in a follow-up chore
options.rationale: Fastest path to v2 files on disk. But 'drafted on stale state' may propagate into downstream consumers (wiki, meta-optimization) before correction.

options.label: Defer all draft values to a separate execution item — this item only lands the schema/code
options.rationale: Clean separation: schema + prompt rendering first, data population second. Downside: two PRs/items where one could suffice; the schema change is easier to validate with populated data.

items.topic: Scope of the team-dependencies CLI command in Action 3
items.context: The command needs to project team→team edges. The conclusion lists three edge sources: (1) agent-membership transitivity via skills, (2) shared-skill coupling, (3) CLI usage ownership. Shipping all three on day 1 vs. starting minimal affects Action 3's effort and testability.

options.label: Ship all 3 edge sources in v1 of the command
options.rationale: Complete dependency picture from day 1. Each edge kind is labeled in the output so consumers can filter. Bigger Action 3 scope but avoids a follow-up.

options.label: Ship agent-membership transitivity only; add shared-skill and CLI usage in a follow-up
options.rationale: Transitivity via skills is the highest-signal relationship and reuses the graph directly. Shared-skill coupling is weaker; CLI ownership needs a 'team-owns-cli' mapping that doesn't exist yet. Smaller, faster first cut.

options.label: Defer the entire dependencies command to a separate research item; do not include Action 3 here
options.rationale: Dependency computation is a distinct design problem; the schema v2 can land without it. But round 1 d3 already resolved to include the command — this would reopen that decision.

plan_updates: Updated conclusion.md: incorporated round 1 resolved decisions (per-file schemaVersion, no team stubs, CLI-only dependencies command) into findings and migration path; corrected Team struct description to current Runtime/Coordination/Execution shape; added Finding 3 (prompt-builder rendering pattern) and Finding 4 (per-member HEARTBEAT.md/RESPONSIBILITIES.md); rewrote Finding 8 to frame dependencies as a projection over the existing api/graph/ infrastructure; expanded Finding 9 migration path to include concrete sub-structs, TeamSchemaVersion constant, test coverage; tightened all three actions with acceptance_allow paths, initiative label, and depends_on relationships.
